Create the whisper worker protocol — persistent Python worker and TypeScript client.

**Files:**
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper-client.ts` — TypeScript client
- `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py` — Python worker process

**whisper-client.ts responsibilities:**
- Spawn whisper_worker.py with configurable model/device/compute args
- Implement line-delimited JSON protocol (worker reads stdin, writes JSONL to stdout)
- Protocol messages: START (model init), FEED (PCM chunk), FINALISE (get transcript), STOP
- Handle partial transcripts: emit events as they arrive
- Handle errors: forward worker stderr/exit code as error events
- Lifecycle: init on recording start, feed PCM frames during recording, finalise on stop, clean exit

**whisper_worker.py responsibilities:**
- Import faster-whisper on startup
- Load model once (device + compute_type from config, with CPU int8 fallback)
- Run a loop: read JSON commands from stdin, write JSON responses to stdout
- FEED accumulates audio, transcribes at configurable cadence
- FINALISE returns the complete transcript
- Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM

**Unit tests (TDD — mock the Python worker process):**
- START message spawns worker and waits for READY response
- FEED messages buffer data and trigger partial transcript callbacks
- FINALISE collects all buffered data and returns final transcript
- STOP sends SHUTDOWN, waits for ACK, verifies clean exit
- Worker stderr/exit code produces error events, never crashes the client

# implement.py parent misclassifies soft-deleted children

## Problem
`implement.py parent <parent-id>` treats a child whose `deletedBy` is set (soft-deleted; `status` remains `open`) as implementable. `_classify_child` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` only checks `status` against `TERMINAL_STATUSES` ({in_review, completed, done, deleted}); it never inspects `deletedBy`. As a result `phase_parent` calls `phase_start` on the soft-deleted child, creates a bogus worktree/branch, claims the item `in_progress`, and stops the chain instead of advancing the parent.

## Reproduction
`wl delete <child>` on a child of an epic sets `deletedBy` but leaves `status: open` (verified with SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X / SA-0MUD5U06J009V0EK, both `deletedBy: plan`). Running `implement.py parent SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0` then started a worktree for SA-0MUD5SYC0002SX5X and set it `in-progress`, even though both real children were `completed`.

## Expected
A child with `deletedBy` set must be treated as terminal (`skip-terminal`): never claimed, never given a worktree, and never allowed to block parent advancement.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_classify_child` treats `deletedBy` (non-empty) as terminal regardless of `status`.
- [ ] `phase_parent` advances a parent whose only non-terminal statuses are soft-deleted children.
- [ ] Soft-deleted children count as terminal when gating in-chain blockers, so a child blocked only by a soft-deleted sibling is still startable (terminal determination must be consistent with `_classify_child`, not status-only).
- [ ] Regression test: a soft-deleted child is skipped and the parent advances.

## Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-07 — plan skill auto-complete path (effort Extra Small / risk Low, approval gate not warranted): added AC3 so the terminal determination used for in-chain blocker gating matches `_classify_child`; traced remaining ACs to the reported bug; no child work items created (below planning threshold).

- None — the pre-check classified this item as below the planning threshold (Extra Small / Low), so no interview questions were asked. Seed intent was taken as authoritative from this work item's description (discovered-from SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0).

# Discord embed composition: pitch, focus, ordering

**Goal.** Extend `discord-notify.js` to compose the embed description with pitch and focus paragraphs in the correct order, with proper fallbacks, and truncate at 4096 characters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **projectDescription resolution.** `projectDescription` is resolved with the same three-layer precedence as `projectName` (`.worklog/config.private.yaml` → `.worklog/config.yaml` → `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`). Config value always wins over generation.
- **Pitch fallback.** When `projectDescription` is unset, the pitch is generated from the leading prose block of `README.md` (before the first `##` heading, capped at ~1000 characters) via the LLM. When generation is unavailable (no API key, LLM error, missing README), the pitch paragraph is omitted.
- **Focus extraction.** `discord-notify.js` extracts the `> **Release focus:** …` marker from the changelog body and uses it as the focus paragraph. The marker is removed from the changelog text sent to Discord so it is not duplicated.
- **Focus omission.** When no focus marker exists in the changelog, the focus paragraph is omitted.
- **Ordered composition.** Description paragraphs are composed in order: (a) project elevator pitch, (b) release focus, (c) project/version line, (d) changelog section.
- **Truncation.** The full composed description is truncated to ≤ 4096 characters (Discord limit).
- **Non-blocking.** All new failure paths (missing config, missing API key, LLM error, missing README, missing focus marker) log info/warning and return without changing the release exit code.
- **Tests.** Comprehensive unit tests: pitch from config, pitch from README/LLM, pitch omitted, focus extraction, focus omitted, paragraph ordering, truncation, config precedence. All LLM/network boundaries injected (no live network).

- `discord-notify.js` (modified — pitch, focus, composition)

## Summary

The audit runner cannot re-audit an item in the terminal `completed`/`done` state: its entry status lifecycle unconditionally claims the item with `wl update <id> --status in_progress` (no `--stage`), and the worklog rejects `in-progress`/`done` as an incompatible status/stage pair.

## Evidence

Reproduced from a clean checkout against a scratch item:

```text
$ wl update <done-item> --status in_progress --json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Invalid status/stage combination: status \"in-progress\" is not compatible with stage \"done\". Allowed stages for status \"in-progress\": intake_complete, plan_complete. Allowed statuses for stage \"done\": completed, deleted."
}
```

The ContextHub compatibility guard (`isStatusStageCompatible`) only whitelists the audit-runner transitional pair for `in-progress` with `in_review`, `idea`, `intake_complete`, and `plan_complete` — not `done`.

This blocks parent SA-0MUJNZ5RN0078B5M AC4: re-auditing the already-`done` SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (child SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6, which forbids reopening the item).

## Desired behaviour

Re-auditing a `completed`/`done` item must work without reopening it. A `done` item is already terminal, so the runner must not attempt the invalid `in-progress`/`done` claim; it should run the audit and let the verdict-driven terminal lifecycle keep/restore `done` (Yes), demote to `open`/`plan_complete` (No), or restore `completed`/`done` (failure).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `cmd_issue` does not issue an invalid `--status in_progress` claim for a `completed`/`done` item.
- [ ] Regression test: auditing a `completed`/`done` item with a `Ready to close: Yes` report completes without the invalid claim and leaves the item `completed`/`done`.
- [ ] Regression test: a `Ready to close: No` re-audit of a `done` item demotes it to `open`/`plan_complete`.
- [ ] Regression test: an infra failure on a `done` item restores `completed`/`done`.
- [ ] Existing lifecycle tests remain green; full suite green.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`cmd_issue` entry claim, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocks SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6 (re-audit SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX).
